{{Quote|The Emperor's Fortress. Once Vitiate's seat of power. Then briefly in the hands of Darth Malgus.|[[Lana Beniko]] to the [[Alliance Commander]]|<ref name="fortress" />}}
During the crisis with [[Darth Malgus]] assisting [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla]] in dismantling the [[Hidden Chain]] and [[Heta Kol]], the [[Alliance Commander]] received news that the reconnaissance team sent to [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]] to uncover Malgus' plans had gone missing so, with [[Lana Beniko]] assisting, the pair '''headed''' to Ilum to uncover this mystery.<ref name="fortress" />

==Prelude==
In [[3640 BBY]], [[Darth Malgus]] stole the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]]'s [[Emperor's Fortress|space fortress]] and broke away from the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] to establish his own empire that would be free of the infighting of the [[Dark Council]] and free to "purify" the galaxy through unrelenting warfare. However, his New Empire's existence was a brought to a [[Battle of Ilum|quick and short end]] by both Republic and Imperial forces alike over [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]], with Malgus presumed dead as the fortress crashed into the planet surface.<ref>{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|The False Emperor}}</ref> However, he would turn up alive during the Empire's [[Invasion of Ossus|invasion]] of [[Ossus]] in [[3628 BBY]].<ref name="Jedi Under Siege">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Jedi Under Siege|[[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]]}}</ref>

Malgus, having forced back into Imperial service through both physical and mental restraints, took his opportunity to desert the Empire while [[Battle of the Meridian Complex|fighting]] atop the [[Meridian Complex]].<ref>{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Objective: Meridian|[[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]}}</ref> He traveled to the ruins of the [[Jedi Enclave]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], where he collected a relic belonging to an unknown Sith called [[Darth Nul]]. It was later noted by the [[Eternal Alliance]] that Malgus had stolen a tome from the Ossus library as well.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Secrets of the Enclave|[[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]}}</ref> 

At some point, Malgus returned to his fortress on Ilum, where he accessed the Emperor's vault inside the station, where he discovered a [[Rakatan]] [[mind prison]] containing the spirit of Darth Nul. Having somehow learned of her history that the Sith Emperor tried to expunge and her ultimate desire to awaken the Force in many on a galactic scale, Malgus sympathized with her beliefs and coerced her into providing the information he required to make her vision a reality, promising to help free her from her prison.<ref name="fortress" />

Malgus then traveled to the [[Temple of Nul]] on [[Elom (planet)/Legends|Elom]] to retrieve [[Darth Nul's holocron]], where he came into conflict with Jedi Master [[Denolm Orr]] and his Padawan [[Sa'har Kateen]], killing Orr but left Kateen to fend for herself.<ref name="Disorder">{{TORweb|url=info/news/article/20220215-0|text="Disorder"|int=Disorder}}</ref> Though he was subsequently captured by the Alliance Commander, he promised that his plan was already in motion, as Kateen had recovered the holocron,<ref name="Ruins of Nul">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=flashpoint|Ruins of Nul}}</ref> leading her on a path to siding with the [[Hidden Chain]]<ref name="LotsDD">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Digging Deeper|Elom}}</ref>, who attempted to exploit the holocron's secrets.<ref name="Ruhnuk">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Showdown on Ruhnuk|[[Ruhnuk]]}}</ref> A remorseful Kateen would later help the Commander steal the holocron from the [[Hidden Chain flagship]], though Kateen was seemingly killed when the ship self-destructed along with her [[Ri'kan Kateen|brother Ri'kan]]. Subsequently, [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla]] led a team of mercenaries to break Malgus out of prison, believing he could lead her to her rival, [[Heta Kol]].<ref name="Sundering">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Sundering|[[Carrick Station]]}}</ref> In response to Vizla's abandonment of her duties as Mandalore, the [[Mandalorian Trat'ade]], represented by [[Arbiter (Mandalorians)|Arbiter]] [[Jekiah Ordo]], traveled to [[Odessen]] to help the Alliance search for both Vizla and Malgus.<ref name="Galactic Threads">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Galactic Threads|[[Odessen]]}}</ref> 

While the Alliance Commander was busy running down a [[Jemala Ha'rangir|Hidden Chain defector]], <ref name="TOR:OK">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|On The Run|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref>, Vizla's accomplice [[Greb Besrik]],<ref name="Hoth Pursuit">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Hoth Pursuit|[[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]}}</ref> and accessing [[Darth Nul's Laboratory|inner sanctum of Nul's temple]],<ref name="Library">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|The Library of Nul|Elom}}</ref>, the Alliance sent a reconnaissance team led by Dr. [[Farrus Belisk]] to locate the Emperor's Fortress on Ilum. As the fortress had a cloaking device based on [[Gree technology]] that made it hard to detect, Belisk's assistant, [[Destom Wuff]], suggested that the fortress's cloak might've been damaged in the crash. Belisk then had his team run down several Gree signatures on Ilum and ultimately isolated the Fortress' Gree technology. Subsequently exploring the ruins, Belisk ordered his team member, [[Ginli Kahraka]], to access the station's records to see if Malgus was looking for data on Rakata technology. But when their astromech, [[D9-28]], plugged into the system, Wuff noted a sudden power fluctuation, which Belisk mistook for an error on Deenine's part, when the power coupler suddenly exploded, killing Kahraka.<ref name="fortress" />

Venturing further into the structure, Belisk and Wuff found another console and began downloading data on the Rakatan [[Foundry (space station)|Foundry]]. Wuff became concerned that the information had compiled when he hadn't even assembled the file index, suspecting a presence, ambiguously referring to as "it", heard them. The survey team soon became aware of the presence, as the station itself seemed to be forcing them to go deeper inside, but every last member was eventually killed off.<ref name="fortress" />

==The mission==
After the Commander completed all three of their missions, [[Lana Beniko]] declared that they had to travel to Ilum, as the survey team had dropped out of contact. As most of the contractors on the team were on loan from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], failing to discern their fate could result in political trouble. However, she stated that finding the team was a secondary priority, as finding the Emperor's Fortress was more important.<ref name="fortress" />

The Commander and Beniko traveled to Ilum and located Belisk's camp. Finding a datapad left at the camp detailing the survey team's efforts on utilizing exclusion protocols on Gree technology, the pair perform the same with the Gree tech in the area and managed to locate the Emperor's Fortress. Upon entering the ruins of Malgus' throne room, the Commander recalled how they were forced to stop Malgus' New Empire from dominating the galaxy. As they explored, they found a deactivated D9-28 and recovered its data log, playing an audio recording of its Kahraka's deaths. Beniko then questioned where the rest of the survey team was. As the Commander suggested they must've gone further into the station, suddenly, a series of electrical arcs opened a nearby door. The pair continued to follow the trail, fighting past wild [[lisk]]s and [[guid]]s while discovering other audio recordings the survey team left behind.<ref name="fortress" />

Eventually, they found Belisk's corpse lying beside a terminal with a dataspike inserted. The Commander observed a power conduit in his hand and speculated he was trying to take the terminal offline. An uncertain Beniko suggested that if they wanted answers, they would have do the opposite. Subsequently reactivating the terminal, holorecordings of Malgus began to play, starting with one of his speeches he made for his New Empire. Subsequent recordings were fragmented, depicting Malgus speaking to someone, contemplating spreading a wave of chaos to grant all power and prove that true strength prevails.<ref name="fortress" />

Suddenly, the same electric arcs burst from the terminal and affected all the deceased survey team members, reanimated them as cyberneurotic zombies, who then attacked the pair. Fighting through the zombies, the pair went further into the station. As they made their way through the power core, Beniko began to sense the presence the survey team spoke of, remarking it was indistinct, but faint. She then spotted another descent cable and hopefully speculated that someone from the survey team survived. Using the descent cable, the pair made their way down, only to be attacked by reactivated Imperial battle droids.<ref name="fortress" />

Eventually, the pair found themselves at the Emperor's vault. The Commander then pointed out that they shouldn't have made it this far, unless something wanted them to. They then spotted at the center of the vault the Rakatan mind trap. As Darth Nul's holocron began to react to the device, Beniko speculated that Malgus sought the prisoner inside. She then forewarned the Commander that whomever was inside the mind trap desired to escaped and would claim their body to do it, and promised to protect them.<ref name="fortress" />

Upon entering the mind prison, the pair discovered the spirit of Darth Nul, who realized they were not Malgus. In turn, the Commander deduced Nul's identity. Initially, Nul denied to be anyone of importance, but Beniko corrected that they were aware of the mark she left on the galaxy and that someone was seeking to use her ideas to burn it down. Nul then explained that the Sith Emperor imprisoned her after learning she planned to awaken the Force in many on a galactic scale, fearing the many would collectively rival his own godlike power. However, Malgus sympathized with her beliefs that both the Jedi and the Sith deny the Force's gifts from those they deemed unworthy and she gave him the information needed to make her vision a reality. She then recalled that Malgus promised her freedom and concluded that he sent the Commander to be her new vessel. Changing from a healthy looking [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] to a decrepit old woman, she then fought against the Commander and Beniko but couldn't defeat them. As she collapsed on the illusory ground, she impotently wailed that she must see her work complete, while the Commander and Beniko escaped.<ref name="fortress" />

Upon returning to the real world, the pair regain their senses as the mind prison suddenly tumbled over and exploded, presumably killing Nul. As the Commander lamented that Nul's obsession with dismantling the Jedi and the Sith ended up destroying her, Beniko reminded that while Nul may be dead, but her legacy isn't; as long as her holocron existed, someone would be able to succeed where she failed.<ref name="fortress" />

==Aftermath==
The Commander and Beniko then returned to Odessen. After watching Jekiah's shuttle returning to the ''[[Spirit of Vengeance II]]'' from Alliance Operations, they suddenly receive a holorecording from [[Darth Jadus]], who revealed that he was responsible for aiding in repairing Nul's droid and fabricated the distress call from Jemala Ha'rangir, remarking he was close to losing his patience. He made clear that Malgus intended to use Nul's machine to awaken the Force on a galactic scale in order to fundamentally upend the Jedi and Sith, while Heta Kol, blind to her own desire to reshape the galaxy, was on course to making Malgus' vision a reality. However, both the Commander and Sa'har managed to steal away the holocron, which is a critical component to the success or failure of Nul's machine; he also shared an image of both a captive Sa'har and Ri'kan meeting Hidden Chain soldiers. His message continued by stating that the Commander was the only one who stood in the way of the inevitable; they can continue to thwart one another or accept Jadus' counsel and have control in what was to come. The message concluded with Jadus telling the Commander to consider their choices carefully and that he would contact them again.<ref name="fortress" />

Once the message had ended, Beniko expressed her surprise at Jadus' involvement, as he would've been her last suspect. She could only speculate that Jadus was seeking revenge against the Sith for exiling him and was going to take the Jedi down too as a bonus, but his endgame was enigmatic. The Commander agreed with Beniko, stating that Jadus had a long time to lay the groundwork for his scheme, but added that he couldn't hide forever.<ref name="fortress" />
